title: The origin of the legumes is a complex paleopolyploid phylogenomic tangle closely associated with the Cretaceous–Paleogene (K–Pg) mass extinction event
authors: Koenen, E.J.M.; Ojeda, D.I.; Bakker, F.T.; Wieringa, J.J.; Kidner, C.; Hardy, O.J.; Pennington, R.T.; Herendeen, P.S.; Bruneau, A.; Hughes, C.E.
note: Phylogenomic analysis explicitly identifies the 65.35 Ma Corral Bluffs material as the oldest unequivocal legume fossil while keeping divergence estimates model-dependent.

title: Early Ordovician sea scorpions from Morocco suggest Cambrian origins and main diversification of Eurypterida
authors: Van Roy, P.; Richards, M.A.; Ortega-Hernández, J.
publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
note: Primary description of unequivocal upper Tremadocian Fezouata eurypterids; the approximately 479 Ma occurrence is a fossil-record bound, not a lineage origin date.

title: Distribution and dispersal history of Eurypterida (Chelicerata)
authors: Tetlie, O.E.
note: Systematic distribution review records a Late Permian Russian occurrence at approximately 250 Ma while noting incomplete taxonomy and sampling.

title: Zygoptera systematics: past, present, and future
authors: Sutherland, K.K.; Carter, B.E.; Abbott, J.C.; et al.
note: Systematic review distinguishes the oldest Serpukhovian Odonatoptera record from the later appearance of modern Odonata.

title: Odonata (dragonflies and damselflies) as a bridge between ecology and evolutionary genomics
authors: Bybee, S.; Córdoba-Aguilar, A.; Duryea, M.C.; et al.
note: Review identifies Saxonagrion minutus at approximately 268 Ma as the earliest modern odonate; this is a fossil minimum rather than an origin estimate.

title: Induced Power Scaling Alone Cannot Explain Griffenfly Gigantism
authors: Ellers, O.; Gordon, B.; Hukill, A.; et al.
note: Functional study summarizes the reviewed first Namurian B record and persistence through at least the end of the Middle Permian; it does not supply an exact extinction date.

title: Revision of Permo-Carboniferous griffenflies based upon new species and redescription of selected poorly known taxa from Eurasia
authors: Nel, A.; Fleck, G.; Garrouste, R.; et al.
note: Systematic redescription of selected griffenfly material; it does not establish exact genus-wide temporal endpoints for Meganeura.

title: Early evolution of beetles regulated by the end-Permian deforestation
authors: Zhao, X.; Yu, Y.; Clapham, M.E.; et al.
note: Integrated fossil dataset identifies Early Permian Tshekardocoleidae as the earliest definite beetles and uses a standardized Asselian bin beginning at 298 Ma.

title: Evolving perspectives in Hymenoptera systematics: Bridging fossils and genomes across time
authors: Zhang, Y.M.; Bossert, S.; Spasojevic, T.
note: Systematic review treats the approximately 242–237 Ma xyelid record as the oldest undisputed hymenopteran fossil minimum, not an order-origin date.

title: Exceptionally Preserved 450-Million-Year-Old Ordovician Ostracods with Brood Care
authors: Siveter, D.J.; Tanaka, G.; Farrell, Ú.C.; et al.
note: Primary description identifies Luprisca as the first unequivocal pre-Silurian ostracod record and cautions against older shell-only assignments.

title: Early Evolution of Phyllocarid Arthropods: Phylogeny and Systematics of Cambrian-Devonian Archaeostracans
authors: Collette, J.H.; Hagadorn, J.W.
note: Phylogenetic and systematic treatment supporting a middle–late Cambrian phyllocarid record.

title: The evolutionary history of Stomatopoda inferred from molecular data
authors: Van Der Wal, C.; Ahyong, S.T.; Ho, S.Y.W.; Lo, N.
note: Fossil-calibration table treats phyllocarids as the oldest malacostracan record at at least 500 Ma; the value is not a crown-divergence date.

title: The Global Fossil Record of Chilopoda
authors: Cadenas-Amaya, O.; Riquelme, F.; Hernández-Patricio, M.; Cupul-Magaña, F.G.
note: Global catalog identifies Upper Silurian Crussolum from Ludford Lane at approximately 418 Ma as the oldest chilopod record.

title: Reconciling Divergent Ages for the Oldest Recorded Air-Breathing Land Animal
authors: Brookfield, M.E.; Catlos, E.J.; Garza, H.
note: Geological age review dates Kampecaris obanensis to 425.5 ± 4.5 Ma; uncertainty remains separate from the display edge.

title: The Silurian-Devonian fossil record of the Myriapoda
authors: Almond, J.E.; Lawson, J.D.
publisher: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
note: Review regards pre-Pridoli records as questionable and recognizes reliable Diplopoda in the latest Silurian to Lower Devonian.

title: A Larval Sea Spider from the Upper Cambrian Orsten of Sweden, and the Phylogenetic Position of Pycnogonids
authors: Waloszek, D.; Dunlop, J.A.
note: Primary study proposes Cambropycnogon as the oldest pycnogonid/chelicerate record; subsequent review leaves its assignment uncertain.

title: New insights into the Devonian sea spiders of the Hunsrück Slate
authors: Sabroux, R.; Garwood, R.J.; Pisani, D.; Donoghue, P.C.J.; Edgecombe, G.D.
note: Table 1 classifies Cambropycnogon only as possibly Pycnogonida, requiring a contested total-group interpretation.

title: Fossil spiders
authors: Selden, P.A.; Penney, D.
note: Systematic fossil-record review supports the Carboniferous spider record while retaining taxonomic and sampling limits.

title: Almost a spider: a 305-million-year-old fossil arachnid and spider origins
authors: Garwood, R.J.; Dunlop, J.A.; Selden, P.A.; et al.
publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
note: Study distinguishes the 305 Ma stem-like Idmonarachne from true spiders and traces Araneae to approximately 315 Ma.

title: Evolutionary trends in Triceratops from the Hell Creek Formation, Montana
authors: Scannella, J.B.; Fowler, D.W.; Goodwin, M.B.; Horner, J.R.
publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
note: A stratigraphically controlled Hell Creek skull sample documents cranial character variation; proposed evolutionary mode remains sensitive to taxon and character treatment.

title: Mites as fossils: forever small?
authors: Sidorchuk, E.A.
note: Review catalogs more than 260 mite fossils from approximately 410 Ma onward and rejects unsupported Ordovician and Permian assignments.

title: Aglaophyton major, a non-vascular land-plant from the Devonian Rhynie Chert
authors: Edwards, D.S.
publisher: Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society
note: Primary re-examination of new and historical material that established Aglaophyton for the former Rhynia major and revised its reconstruction and conducting-strand interpretation.

title: Transfer cells in Horneophyton lignieri illuminate the origin of vascular tissues in land plants
authors: Kenrick, P.; Long, E.J.
note: Open-access primary study of 24 Horneophyton-bearing sections; three NHMUK slides were selected for white-light and confocal imaging plus three-dimensional modelling.

title: A high-precision U–Pb age constraint on the Rhynie Chert Konservat-Lagerstätte: time scale and other implications
authors: Parry, S.F.; Noble, S.R.; Crowley, Q.G.; Wellman, C.H.
note: Open repository version records an ID-TIMS U–Pb zircon age of 411.5 ± 1.3 Ma from andesite in the Rhynie Outlier; the atlas uses the uncertainty interval only as a locality-age bound.

title: Galeaspid anatomy and the origin of vertebrate paired appendages
authors: Gai, Z.; Li, Q.; Ferrón, H.G.; Keating, J.N.; Wang, J.; Donoghue, P.C.J.; Zhu, M.
note: Primary description of articulated Tujiaaspis material from the Huixingshao Formation; CFD lift results are model outputs and do not measure whole-animal swimming performance.

title: Broad snouted cladoselachian with sensory specialization at the base of modern chondrichthyans
authors: Klug, C.; Coates, M.I.; Frey, L.; Greif, M.; Jobbins, M.; Pohle, A.; Lagnaoui, A.; Haouz, W.B.; Ginter, M.
note: Open-access primary description of Maghriboselache mohamezanei from several Moroccan Famennian specimens, including CT-preserved neurocrania and a time-calibrated phylogenetic analysis; a 2024 correction is noted by the publisher.

title: A new operculate symmoriiform chondrichthyan from the Late Mississippian Fayetteville Shale (Arkansas, United States)
authors: Bronson, A.W.; Pradel, A.; Denton, J.S.S.; Maisey, J.G.
note: Primary description and CT-based phylogenetic study of the partial holotype AMNH FF 20509; the specimen supplies direct evidence for an endoskeletal operculum but not a complete body or clade-wide range.

title: A complete insect from the Late Devonian period
authors: Garrouste, R.; Clément, G.; Nel, P.; Engel, M.S.; Grandcolas, P.; D'Haese, C.; Lagebro, L.; Denayer, J.; Gueriau, P.; Lafaite, P.; Olive, S.; Prestianni, C.; Nel, A.
note: Primary description of the nearly complete Strudiella devonica specimen from Upper Devonian freshwater sediments at Strud, Belgium; the original study interpreted it as an insect.

title: Is Strudiella a Devonian insect?
authors: Hörnschemeyer, T.; Haug, J.T.; Béthoux, O.; Beutel, R.G.; Charbonnier, S.; Hegna, T.A.; Koch, M.; Rust, J.; Wedmann, S.; Bradler, S.; Willmann, R.
note: Primary re-investigation of Strudiella that rejects the original insect identification and cautions against interpreting poorly preserved Devonian arthropods as insects.

title: Under cover at pre-angiosperm times: A cloaked phasmatodean insect from the Early Cretaceous Jehol biota
authors: Wang, M.; Béthoux, O.; Bradler, S.; Jacques, F.M.B.; Cui, Y.; Ren, D.
note: Primary description of one female and two male Cretophasmomima melanogramma specimens from the Yixian Formation, dated to approximately 126 ± 4 Ma, including the stem-Phasmatodea diagnosis and proposed leaf mimicry.
